frontmatter.description: It enables developers to create, edit, convert, and render Excel files programmatically without requiring Microsoft Excel to be installed.
frontmatter.title: Use Cases

blocks.content: Aspose.Cells for Python via .NET is a high-code API for processing Excel spreadsheets using Python. It enables developers to create, edit, convert, and render Excel files programmatically without requiring Microsoft Excel to be installed.

The library supports high-quality file format conversion and rendering, including exporting worksheets, charts, and specific data ranges to PDF or image formats. This makes it ideal for generating reports, dashboards, and data exports in standardized, shareable formats.

Aspose.Cells for Python processes Excel files through the `Workbook` class, which serves as the central entry point for loading, editing, and saving spreadsheet data. It supports opening files from paths, streams, or encrypted sources by accepting a file path or file-like object alongside optional `LoadOptions` to specify format and security settings. Once loaded, the workbook exposes collections like `worksheets`, `custom_document_properties`, and `custom_theme`, enabling programmatic access to content, metadata, and formatting.

The library calculates formulas in-memory using Excel’s native engine, ensuring accurate results for built-in and custom functions without requiring Microsoft Excel. It also supports rendering to images, printing to physical or virtual printers, and saving to multiple formats—including XLSX, XLS, CSV, PDF, and HTML—while preserving layout and styling. This makes Aspose.Cells suitable for server-side automation where reliability and consistency across environments are critical.

import os
from pathlib import Path
import aspose_cells_foss as cells


def get_data_dir():
    return (
        Path(__file__).parent
        / ".."
        / ".."
        / ".."
        / "Data"
        / "Files"
        / "Handling"
        / "OpeningEncryptedExcelFiles"
    )


def run():
    data_dir = get_data_dir()
    load_options = cells.LoadOptions()
    load_options.password = "1234"
    wb_encrypted = cells.Workbook(str(data_dir / "encryptedBook.xls"), load_options)
    print("Encrypted excel file opened successfully!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    run()

Aspose.Cells enables granular formatting control over Excel worksheets without requiring Microsoft Excel to be installed. This example demonstrates how to apply and preserve the single quote prefix on cell values using `StyleFlag` and `Style` objects. The single quote prefix is commonly used in Excel to force text interpretation of numeric-looking values, and Aspose.Cells preserves this formatting behavior programmatically.

import os
import aspose_cells_foss as cells

def get_source_directory():
    return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(".", "..", "..", "Data", "01_SourceDirectory"))

def get_output_directory():
    return os.path.abspath(os.path.join(".", "..", "..", "Data", "02_OutputDirectory"))

def run_preserve_single_quote_prefix_of_cell_value_or_range():
    # Create workbook
    workbook = cells.Workbook()

    # Access first worksheet
    worksheet = workbook.worksheets[0]

    # Access cell A1
    cell = worksheet.cells.get("A1")

    # Put some text in cell, it does not have Single Quote at the beginning
    cell.put_value("Text")
    style = cell.get_style()
    print(f"Quote Prefix of Cell A1: {style.quote_prefix}")

    # Put some text in cell, it has Single Quote at the beginning
    cell.put_value("'Text")
    style = cell.get_style()
    print(f"Quote Prefix of Cell A1: {style.quote_prefix}")

    print()
    print("When StyleFlag.QuotePrefix is False, it means, do not update the value of Cell.Style.QuotePrefix.")
    print("Similarly, when StyleFlag.QuotePrefix is True, it means, update the value of Cell.Style.QuotePrefix.")
    print()

    # Create an empty style
    style = workbook.create_style()

    # Create style flag - set StyleFlag.QuotePrefix as false
    flag = cells.StyleFlag()
    flag.quote_prefix = False

    # Create a range consisting of single cell A1
    rng = worksheet.cells.create_range("A1")

    # Apply the style to the range
    rng.apply_style(style, flag)

    # Access the style of cell A1
    style = cell.get_style()
    print(f"Quote Prefix of Cell A1: {style.quote_prefix}")

    # Create an empty style
    style = workbook.create_style()

    # Create style flag - set StyleFlag.QuotePrefix as true
    flag = cells.StyleFlag()
    flag.quote_prefix = True

    # Apply the style to the range
    rng.apply_style(style, flag)

    # Access the style of cell A1
    style = cell.get_style()
    print(f"Quote Prefix of Cell A1: {style.quote_prefix}")

    print("PreserveSingleQuotePrefixOfCellValueOrRange executed successfully.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_preserve_single_quote_prefix_of_cell_value_or_range()

Aspose.Cells enables robust spreadsheet automation in Python, supporting chart creation, pivot table manipulation, and worksheet formatting via a clean API. Developers familiar with openpyxl in Python can transition smoothly, leveraging Aspose.Cells for advanced features like 3D chart formatting, custom number patterns, and range operations without relying on Excel installation.
